content.value_statement: Code review feedback can be unclear, conflicting, or technically wrong. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to verify feedback before acting.
actual_capabilities: Provides a step-by-step pattern for reading, verifying, evaluating, responding, and implementing review feedback.
Defines when to ask for clarification before changing code.
Guides skeptical evaluation of external reviewer suggestions against the current codebase.
Prioritizes blocking issues, simple fixes, complex fixes, and regression checks.
Shows concise response examples for correct, unclear, and technically flawed feedback.
Advises replying to GitHub inline review threads instead of top-level comments.
limitations: Does not execute review fixes by itself.
Does not validate reviewer claims without access to the repository and tests.
Does not replace human architectural decisions.
May be too strict for teams that prefer more social acknowledgment.

use_cases.title: Triage Pull Request Feedback
use_cases.description: Sort review comments by clarity, risk, and implementation order before changing code.

use_cases.title: Check External Suggestions
use_cases.description: Evaluate outside reviewer advice against existing behavior, platform support, and project constraints.

use_cases.title: Coach Review Responses
use_cases.description: Prepare concise technical replies that explain verified fixes, uncertainty, or evidence-based pushback.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify Review Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to restate each review item, identify unclear points, and ask only the necessary clarification questions.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Before Implementing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill on this pull request feedback. Check whether each suggestion matches the codebase before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Push Back With Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for questionable external feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate external reviewer comments. For any incorrect suggestion, prepare concise technical pushback with codebase evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Item Review Resolution
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for many comments across a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to triage all review comments, order fixes by risk, test each change, and prepare inline GitHub replies.

output_examples.input: A reviewer says to remove legacy support, but the project may still need it.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks supported platforms, finds the compatibility reason, and asks whether to keep support or change the requirement.

output_examples.input: A review lists six issues, but two are ambiguous.
output_examples.output: The assistant pauses implementation, summarizes understood items, and asks for clarification on the ambiguous items.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks for a large metrics feature that appears unused.
output_examples.output: The assistant searches for usage, reports no callers, and asks whether to remove the unused endpoint instead.

best_practices: Clarify ambiguous feedback before editing files.
Verify reviewer claims against tests, code paths, and project constraints.
Implement review fixes one item at a time and test each change.
anti_patterns: Do not accept feedback only to sound agreeable.
Do not implement unclear multi-item feedback in partial batches.
Do not add unused features only because they sound more complete.

faq.question: Does this skill automate code changes?
faq.answer: No. It guides the assistant to evaluate feedback and plan changes before implementation.

faq.question: Can it help with external reviewer comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages checking external suggestions against the real codebase and existing decisions.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub review replies?
faq.answer: Yes. It advises replying in inline review threads when addressing GitHub comments.

faq.question: Will it always push back on reviewers?
faq.answer: No. It pushes back only when evidence shows the suggestion is unclear, wrong, or harmful.

faq.question: Is it useful for simple typo fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It places simple fixes after blocking issues and before complex refactors.

faq.question: What tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
